accident_report:
Vehicles are traveling on a straight, uphill, one-way roadway with three lanes (lane 1 on the right, lane 3 on the left) and a wide shoulder on the right side. At the initial state, V1 is in lane 2, positioned slightly ahead of the others, moving uphill at 85 km/h with a steady throttle, intending to maintain speed. V2 follows V1 in the same lane at a distance of approximately 8 meters, traveling at 95 km/h, exhibiting a clear tailgating condition and intending to overtake. V3 is in lane 3, slightly behind V2, moving at 70 km/h due to reduced traction on the wet road surface, maintaining a cautious steady speed. V4 is on the wide shoulder to the right of lane 1, traveling at 100 km/h, attempting to bypass slower traffic and intending to merge back into the main lanes. All vehicles are operating at night, with limited visibility and reduced road friction due to a wet surface.

As the scenario develops, V2 closes the gap rapidly with V1 due to the significant speed difference and insufficient following distance. Because of the uphill gradient, V1 slightly reduces speed to 80 km/h to maintain engine load stability, further exacerbating the closing rate. V2 reacts late due to limited nighttime visibility and the short headway, initiating a moderate braking maneuver. Simultaneously, V4 accelerates along the shoulder and attempts an illegal merge into lane 2, targeting the space between V1 and V2. Due to the wet road, V4’s lateral maneuver causes reduced tire grip, resulting in a slightly unstable trajectory as it cuts in.

V2, already braking, is forced to increase braking intensity to avoid V4, reducing speed abruptly from 95 km/h to 60 km/h. This sharp deceleration on the wet surface causes V2’s rear wheels to experience partial loss of traction. V3, observing the sudden deceleration of V2 ahead and the lateral intrusion of V4, attempts to brake and steer slightly left within lane 3 to maintain distance, reducing speed from 70 km/h to 50 km/h. However, due to the large speed differential and delayed perception in low visibility, V3 cannot fully compensate.

The critical interaction occurs when V4 completes its cut-in maneuver but occupies insufficient longitudinal space, forcing V2 into emergency braking. The wet surface amplifies stopping distance for both V2 and V3. V2 narrowly avoids colliding with V4 but decelerates sharply enough to create an unavoidable hazard for V3. V3, unable to reduce speed sufficiently in time, collides with the rear of V2 at approximately 45 km/h, forming the first impact in the sequence.

The final result is a rear-end collision between V3 and V2 in lane 2, triggered by the combined effects of illegal cut-in by V4, excessive speed difference, tailgating behavior of V2, reduced friction from the wet road, and limited nighttime visibility. V1 continues forward with minor influence, while V4 stabilizes ahead after the merge.
